stem: Diya studies the expression $2n+1$ for whole-number values of $n$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies the parity of $2n+1$?

options.text: $2n+1$ is a letter-number label only, with no parity test.
$2n+1$ is always odd for every whole number $n$.
The printed coefficient $2$ alone settles the parity.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: 2n is always even, so 2n+1 is always one more than an even number and stays odd for every whole number n.

teacher.key_rationale: 2n is always even, so 2n+1 is always odd. Treating the expression as a bare label or reading parity from the coefficient 2 alone misses that forced odd form.
